static_traits.name: Li Weiya
static_traits.social_status: Has a small circle of close friends to rely on, but because of shame and guilt about fast food, has reduced gatherings with friends in fast-food settings, and relationships are affected
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychotherapy or psychiatric visits
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, able to notice and Reflect on one's own thought patterns; emotional attitude fairly neutral, but shame and self-blame themes recur in speech

basic_info.main_problem: Because of society's stereotype of fast food as 'unhealthy and low-class', I feel ashamed of liking McDonald's.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent guilt and shame are affecting overall physical and mental health; hoping to ease these emotions through counseling and change negative thoughts about fast food.
growth_experiences: In High school, some popular classmates would mock people who ate fast food; the client associated eating fast food with 'being looked down upon, low-class', and the shame formed in adolescence and continues to this day.

core_beliefs: I am undisciplined, an inferior person
My value depends on others' evaluations of my dietary choices

special_situations.event: A friend suggests gathering at a fast food restaurant
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I eat fast food with them, others will think I have no taste, lack self-discipline, and am a 'low-class' person
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Finds excuses to avoid dinners, or only orders food that 'looks healthier' to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will look down on me

special_situations.event: Ordering and eating alone at McDonald's
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I enjoy fast food, it means I am a bad person / an undisciplined person
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Formulates stricter diet rules and restricts eating; afterwards blames oneself to 'make up for it'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am truly terrible; this shows I am a bad person

special_situations.event: Seeing negative comments about fast food on social media or in real life, or recalling being mocked in High school
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they laugh at people who eat fast food, then all fast-food eaters will be looked down on
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids related discussions and content, hides her liking for fast food
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: People who eat fast food are all looked down upon, and so am I

special_situations.event: At work, thinks about having recently eaten fast food and worries about her image being damaged
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If colleagues or clients knew I eat fast food, they would negate my professionalism and value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Controls more forcefully in diet and conceals it; overworks at the job to 'compensate'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My professional image will be affected by this

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted by peers and society and respected for one's real preferences
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being shamed, looked down upon, and then excluded
defense_goal: Lowers the risk of being looked down on by others through avoidance and self-harshness
Maintains a safe distance from others to avoid being humiliated again

object_relations.self_representation: A shamed person easily judged as 'low-class/undisciplined'
object_relations.object_representation: Others / groups with judgment and contempt

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to discuss or display their real dietary preferences, or when sensing the possible evaluation of others
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will mock or despise me like classmates in the past
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Reflecting feelings in a gentle, validating tone, using probing questions to Clarification evidence (such as 'what cues lead you to infer they will look down on you?'), reducing judgmental overtones, offering emotional support.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When shame and guilt well up and are hard to bear
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Expressing these feelings would shame me more; better to push them down
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Slow the rate of speech, invite naming the emotions and bodily sensations, provide a frame of permission and acceptance ('we can look at these feelings together safely'), and encourage exposure within the tolerable range.

manifestations: Struggles between 'society's evaluation of fast food' and 'one's true preferences', finding it hard to take responsibility for their own choices
Replacing personal choice with rigid rules (must be completely healthy, cannot eat 'low-class' food)
outcomes: Avoidance of social and eating situations

manifestations: Avoids going to fast-food restaurants with friends out of shame
Unwilling to reveal true distress to close friends, fearing being looked down upon
outcomes: Support resources not yet activated, Increased subjective sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Internalizing the social judgment 'fast food = unhealthy = low-class' as a self-evaluation standard
Demanding of oneself 'should eat completely healthy, cannot eat fast food'

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on.
manifestations: Assuming others will look down on one's fast-food choices without clear evidence
Assuming others' disapproval in social settings, thus avoiding participation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Strict self-restraint and self-blame regarding diet and image
Worrying that once 'out of control' one will be negated, thus avoiding expressing true preferences

positive_force: Has a small circle of friends to rely on as potential support resources
Has a clear motivation and willingness to change her way of thinking and reduce shame
Able to identify and name one's own cognitive biases (such as overgeneralization, mental filtering)
Willing to try arranging diet in a more balanced, moderate way
negative_force: Internalizes social stereotypes, directly linking food choices to self-worth
Mind reading and catastrophizing thinking, presetting being looked down on and rejected by others
Black-and-white self-demands and rigid dietary rules
Avoids socializing situations, leading to isolation and Reinforcement of the shame cycle
Repeated self-blame and guilt, undermining concentration and self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids gatherings and socializing with friends at fast-food settings
antecedent: A friend suggests gathering at a fast food restaurant
Thinking about others' possible negative evaluations
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizing the High school experience of being mocked by peers along with social stereotypes, fearing being looked down upon
target_behavior.function: Avoiding judgment, briefly reducing shame and Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Strained and distant interpersonal relationships, support resources hard to obtain

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive guilt and self-blame after eating fast food
antecedent: Seeing or thinking of others' negative evaluations of fast food
target_behavior.core_reason: Black-and-white and overgeneralization cognition, equating a single dietary choice with 'I am a bad/inferior person'
target_behavior.function: Maintains superficial control over image and self-discipline through self-punishment
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired self-esteem, increased emotional distress, difficulty forming a sustainable balanced diet

target_behavior.behavior: At work, distracted by worrying about a 'low-class impression'
antecedent: When colleagues or clients discuss topics such as health and taste
target_behavior.core_reason: Mind reading and catastrophizing, Anticipation that others will negate one's professionalism
target_behavior.function: Maintaining 'preventive' vigilance through worrying to avoid being negated
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased concentration and impaired performance, further aggravating Self-denial
